title: European Commission Approves eCAUSIS Results as Creotech Quantum Prepares QKD System for Commercial Rollout - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The European Commission approved completion of the ~€6.98M eCAUSIS EuroQCI project coordinated by Warsaw-listed Creotech Quantum (GPW: CTQ), moving its PCIe DV-QKD module into commercial production with a 2026 launch, 1,000 units/year initial capacity and a 10,000 units/year scale target.

insights.claim: The European Commission formally approved completion of the eCAUSIS project, moving Creotech Quantum's proprietary discrete-variable QKD (DV-QKD) platform from R&D into commercial production.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Technical and financial sign-off de-risks CTQ's transition to a revenue-generating product company.
insights.locator: Warsaw-listed quantum technology developer Creotech Quantum

insights.claim: eCAUSIS was executed under Horizon Europe, the Digital Europe Programme (Project 101091564) and the EuroQCI initiative, positioning Creotech's QKD to supply terrestrial, metropolitan and cross-border EuroQCI networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: EuroQCI build-out is a sovereign-demand tailwind for European QKD suppliers.
insights.locator: Following its corporate spin-off from Creotech

insights.claim: eCAUSIS had a total budget of €6,977,626.81 (~$8M) with €4,523,868.99 (~$5.155M) of EU grant funding.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows the modest scale of EU grant funding underwriting QKD industrialization.

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum's share was €4.18M in eligible costs funded up to €3.13M; Fraunhofer HHI received €1.16M to develop 1300 nm InGaAs SPAD detectors with CMOS active-quenching ICs, and AIT received €254K for its ETSI-compliant AURORA key management and SDN suite.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Grant funding offset most of CTQ's development cost, limiting dilution risk for the product launch.

insights.claim: The eCAUSIS system is an interoperable DV-QKD PCIe hardware module using the decoy-state BB84 protocol, with platform-independent software aligned to ETSI certification frameworks and Common Criteria.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A PCIe form factor and certification alignment lower integration barriers for telecom and government buyers.

insights.claim: Creotech Quantum plans a 2026 commercial market launch with initial capacity of 1,000 QKD modules per year and potential expansion to 10,000 units annually via a European supply chain.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Capacity targets give a yardstick for future CTQ revenue; watch for EuroQCI orders that fill it.
insights.locator: Following its corporate spin-off from Creotech

insights.claim: After its spin-off from Creotech Instruments S.A., Creotech Quantum holds all IP and commercialization rights to the eCAUSIS results.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Clean IP ownership means project economics accrue to the listed CTQ entity rather than the parent.
